entries.title: Psalms 109:1
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: God - The author and matter of all my praises.

entries.title: Psalms 109:4
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Adversaries - They requite my love with enmity, as it is explained ver. 5.

entries.title: Psalms 109:6
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: A wicked man - Who will rule him with rigour and cruelty. Satan - To accuse him; for this was the place and posture of accusers in the Jewish courts.

entries.title: Psalms 109:7
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Sin - Because it is not from his heart.

entries.title: Psalms 109:10
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Desolate places - Into which they are fled for fear and shame.

entries.title: Psalms 109:11
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Catch - Heb. ensnare, take away not only by oppression but also by cunning artificers. Stranger - Who hath no right to his goods.

entries.title: Psalms 109:17
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Delighted not - In desiring and promoting the welfare of others.

entries.title: Psalms 109:18
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Garment - Which a man wears constantly. Like water - Water in the cavity of the belly, between the bowels, is almost certain death. And oil soaking into any of the bones, will soon utterly destroy it.

entries.title: Psalms 109:20
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: That speak evil against my soul - With design to take away my life.

entries.title: Psalms 109:21
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Is good - Above the mercy of all the creatures.

entries.title: Psalms 109:23
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: When - Towards the evening, when the sun is setting. The locust - Which is easily driven away with every wind.
